create.name: Ani Rinchen Khandro
create.bio:
Ani Rinchen Khandro is a Buddhist nun in the Karma Kagyu school of Tibetan Buddhism who has led Kagyu Samye Dzong Edinburgh, a meditation centre on Bernard Street in Leith, since she was asked to found it in 2008 by Akong Tulku Rinpoche and Lama Yeshe Losal Rinpoche of Samye Ling. She trained for a decade at Samye Ling in the Scottish Borders, where she also handled the monastery's public relations and fundraising, and from 2003 spent the customary three years and more in closed retreat at the women's retreat house on Holy Island, off Arran. She later wrote the monastery's fortieth-anniversary history.

Her teaching is classical and practical: the four thoughts that turn the mind, refuge, karma, the Four Noble Truths, the lives and songs of Milarepa and the Kagyu masters, and the down-to-earth advice of Akong Rinpoche, always paired with sitting meditation. She also teaches qigong as a gentle moving practice alongside the Dharma. Many of her monthly study sessions are filmed and shared free online with their readings, and recordings of her talks are sold for a small fee to support the centre. She serves as the University of Edinburgh's honorary Buddhist chaplain and represents Buddhism in the city's interfaith work.

courses.title: Audio Teaching: The Four Preliminary Foundations – Part 1: Precious Human Life
courses.description: An MP3 recording of her talk on the first of the four thoughts that turn the mind towards practice: the rare opportunity of a human life. The small fee covers recording costs for the centre.

courses.title: Audio Teaching: The Four Preliminary Foundations – Part 3: Karma, Cause and Effect
courses.description: An MP3 recording of her session on karma, explaining how actions shape experience and why this matters for daily practice.

courses.title: Audio Teaching: The Four Preliminary Foundations – Part 4: Samsara
courses.description: An MP3 recording of the last talk in her series on the four thoughts, looking at the restless cycle of conditioned existence and the wish to be free of it.

free_resources.title: Discovering Buddhism (online course)
free_resources.description: Her free three-part filmed introduction to Buddhism, from the life of the Buddha to what his teaching can mean in a modern life.

free_resources.title: The Songs of Milarepa (online course)
free_resources.description: A free filmed study and meditation series on the songs of the Tibetan yogi Milarepa, with downloadable readings for each session.

free_resources.title: Akong Rinpoche: Restoring the Balance (online course)
free_resources.description: A free filmed series in which she works through Akong Rinpoche's book Restoring the Balance, one theme per session, with practical reflection.

flags: Email is the centre's office inbox (info@edinburgh.samye.org), published on her teacher page and in the site footer; she is the centre's director.

All videos are on the centre's YouTube channel (Kagyu Samye Dzong Edinburgh), not a channel of her own; each one is a course session or practice led by her (the course pages name her as teacher). youtube_url left null for that reason.
'Ani' is the Tibetan honorific for a nun and is how she is known publicly, so it is kept in the name and slug.
Kagyu Samye Dzong Edinburgh and Samye Ling are not Spiritpedia listings; teaches_at is empty.
